title: Ultrafast quantum gate operations in a Kramers-Henneberger atom Qubit
authors: A. Tasnim Aynul, C. Li, L. Cruz Rodriguez, C. Figueira de Morisson Faria
abstract: We propose and demonstrate the Kramers-Henneberger KH) atom as a novel qubit platform for ultrafast single-qubit gate operations. In the KH frame, the time-averaged strong laser field engineers a double-well potential whose two lowest eigenstates define the qubit basis, so that the computational structure is created and maintained by the driving field itself. A weak resonant control field drives coherent gate operations: full time-dependent Schrödinger equation simulations with the complete time-dependent KH potential confirm a Z gate and S gate of the order of femtoseconds, six orders of magnitude faster than laser-driven superconducting qubit gates. Decoherence characterisation gives longer decoherence times than those required for the gate operations. The complete six-gate single-qubit set is demonstrated in the time-averaged two-level limit, with strong agreement between the full and time-averaged descriptions confirming that fidelity is limited by structured leakage rather than stochastic decoherence. In principle, this is an error channel suppressible through pulse engineering. These results constitute the first demonstration of coherent single-qubit gates in a strong-field setting, with a clear pathway toward attosecond-scale operations.
summary: The paper introduces the Kramers-Henneberger atom as a promising, ultrafast platform for quantum computing. By engineering the potential using intense laser fields, they demonstrated coherent single-qubit gates (Z and S) operating on femtosecond timescales. This work suggests a clear pathway toward attosecond-scale quantum operations limited by structured leakage rather than environmental decoherence.
main_problem: The authors propose using the Kramers-Henneberger (KH) atom as a novel platform to achieve ultrafast single-qubit gate operations.
main_result: They demonstrated coherent Z and S gates on femtosecond timescales, which is six orders of magnitude faster than current superconducting qubit gates.
method: The study relies on solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation (TDSE) in both the length gauge and a transformed KH frame.
model_or_system: The physical system is an electron governed by the dynamics within a strong, time-varying laser field, modeled using the KH potential. The qubit basis is defined by the two lowest eigenstates engineered by the strong driving field itself.
key_observables: Gate fidelity, gate operation timescales (femtoseconds), and decoherence times.
important_parameters: Strong field parameters ($\epsilon_{0s} = 5.0$ a.u., $\omega_s = 0.7$ a.u.) and weak control field frequencies ($\omega_w$).
main_assumptions: The fidelity is limited by structured leakage rather than stochastic decoherence, suggesting the process can be error-suppressed via pulse engineering.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the KH atom as a qubit platform, derives the Hamiltonian in different gauges (length and KH frame), simulates gate operations using TDSE solvers, and compares results between full time-dependent and time-averaged descriptions to confirm feasibility.
why_interesting: This work proposes an entirely new physical mechanism—utilizing strong field dressing to define a qubit basis—for achieving quantum gates at unprecedented speeds, bridging attosecond physics with quantum computation.
